declared_proposition: For any 0-1 sequence a_n, F(r)=sum a_n r^n is unbounded as r tends to one from below if and only if the support of a is infinite. Applied to the twin-prime indicator, unboundedness of the actual Abel transform is exactly equivalent to the Twin Prime Conjecture. The quantitative TICKET-218 condition liminf F(1-1/X)/(X/log^2 X)>1/2 is sufficient but not a necessary qualitative infinitude criterion: the infinite odd support n_j=2^j+1 has F(1-1/X)=O(log X) and hence normalized liminf zero. Moreover, for any support count T(X), F(1-1/X)>=T(X)/4 for X>=2.
mathematical_argument: Finite support makes F bounded by its support size. For infinite support, choose any K supported indices; their finite partial sum tends to K as r tends to one, so F is unbounded. For n_j=2^j+1, there are O(log X) terms below X, while the terms above X are at most a convergent sum of exp(-2^k), giving F=O(log X). Finally, for n<=X and X>=2, (1-1/X)^n>=(1-1/X)^X>=1/4, proving the finite lower certificate. This refutes necessity only for abstract binary supports, not the Hardy-Littlewood prediction for actual twins.

reproducible_computation.qualitative_equivalence: infinitely many twin primes iff the actual twin Abel transform is unbounded
reproducible_computation.no_go_scope: The sparse sequence is not a model of the primes and does not disprove the TICKET-218 condition for actual twins. It proves only that requiring a Hardy-Littlewood-scale coefficient is an overstrong route to qualitative infinitude.

discarded_route: requiring a positive Hardy-Littlewood-scale Abel liminf as though it were necessary for qualitative twin infinitude
remaining_gap: No parity-sensitive argument proves that the actual twin-prime Abel transform is unbounded, or equivalently that infinitely many dyadic blocks contain a twin.
claim_boundary: No Twin Prime proof or last-twin counterexample. The density-scale requirement is demoted to a sufficient quantitative route; qualitative Abel unboundedness remains open and equivalent to infinitude.
